deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a printed page, not a manuscript leaf. It is the first page (p. 377; the '35' at the foot is the printer's signature mark, not the page number) of 'Nachrichten von der G. A. Universität und der Königl. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen', No. 21, 9 December 1863.

The page reports the society's anniversary meeting of 5 December 1863:
- The society celebrated its foundation day for the twelfth time in its second century. It was founded in 1751, so 1863 is the 112th anniversary.
- G. Waitz gave a memorial lecture on Jacob Grimm, to appear in vol. XI of the Abhandlungen.
- The permanent secretary, Ober-Medicinalrath F. Wöhler, then began the annual report:
  - The directorate rotates yearly among the three oldest members. At Michaelmas 1862 it passed from Ewald (historical-philological class) to Hofrath Marx (physical class). At Michaelmas 1863 it passed to Wilhelm Weber (mathematical class).
  - Since July 1862 the society held 13 sessions, at which 72 larger and smaller papers were read or presented. The larger ones appear in vol. XI of the Abhandlungen; the smaller ones, some only in extract, appear in the Nachrichten.

Show-through of p. 378 (the obituary of Mitscherlich) is visible in mirror image. Two pencil archival annotations appear: 'Riemann ?' (top left) and the folio number '10' (right margin).

The leaf was presumably filed in the 'R.Primzahlen' bundle because it was found with Riemann's papers. Possibly he used it as scrap paper or kept it for this report, which as a member would concern him. The archivist's query 'Riemann ?' shows the attribution or relevance was uncertain. Nothing on this side bears on prime numbers or the zeta function.

results.what: Printed annual report of the Göttingen Royal Society of Sciences (Nachrichten 1863, No. 21); no mathematical content
results.usually_credited_to: F. Wöhler (secretary's report), printed in the Göttinger Nachrichten

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed society bulletin page with no mathematics and no Riemann handwriting on this side. Its presence in the bundle is purely archival.

checkable.asserts: 1863 is the 112th anniversary of the society's founding in 1751, i.e. the 'twelfth time in the second century', as the text says.

transcription_corrections: The pencil note at top left reads 'Riemann ?' (possibly 'Riemann 3'). It is an archivist's annotation, not part of the print.
The '35' at the bottom is the printer's signature (Bogen) number; the page number is 377, consistent with the next page being '— 378 —'.
The marginal '10' is the archival folio number (Bl. 10).
'O. M. R.' is the abbreviation for Ober-Medicinal-Rath (Wöhler's title).
Otherwise the machine transcription matches the print.
